warrants.claim: formalises
formalises

formalises the theorem at the shift mu = 0, for the operator with b = 0 and c >= 0 almost everywhere on an arbitrary bounded Omega, over the solution space H_0^1(Omega) that Evans also takes: every f in L^2(Omega) admits a unique weak solution, with the a-priori bound ‖u‖_{H_0^1} <= (C_P + 1)/lambda · ‖f‖_{L^2}. Evans reaches gamma = 0 for exactly these coefficients in the Examples following the theorem, and states no bound. The Poincare constant is quantified before the datum, so it depends on Omega alone. dirichlet_weak_solution carries the same locator for the pure Dirichlet form

formalises clause (i), the dichotomy, with the compactness of opK as a hypothesis rather than as a consequence of Rellich-Kondrachov: either the homogeneous problem has a nonzero weak solution in H_0^1(Omega), or every continuous functional on H_0^1(Omega) is the datum of a unique weak solution. Evans takes f in L^2(U), where the declaration takes any element of the dual, which is the H^{-1} form Evans records under Mapping H_0^1 to H^{-1} after §6.2.2 Theorem 3. fredholm_alternative_of_bounded is the same statement with the compactness discharged
formalises
formalises

formalises the finite-dimensionality half of clause (ii): the space N of weak solutions of the homogeneous problem, taken in H_0^1(Omega), is finite-dimensional. Evans states it under alternative (beta); the declaration states it unconditionally, which is vacuous under (alpha), where N is trivial. The compactness of opK is a hypothesis rather than a consequence of Rellich-Kondrachov

formalises the index half of clause (ii): the space N* of weak solutions of the transpose problem and the space N of weak solutions of the homogeneous problem, both taken in H_0^1(Omega), have the same finite dimension. Evans states it under alternative (beta); the declaration states it unconditionally, both ranks being zero under (alpha). The compactness of opK is a hypothesis rather than a consequence of Rellich-Kondrachov
formalises

formalises the theorem with the compactness of opK as a hypothesis rather than as a consequence of Rellich-Kondrachov: for lambda outside Sigma there is C > 0 with ‖u‖_{L^2(Omega)} <= C · ‖f‖_{L^2(Omega)} for every f in L^2(Omega) and every u in H_0^1(Omega) satisfying the weak identity for Lu = lambda u + f. Evans quantifies over the unique weak solution, which is the same element once §6.2.3 Theorem 5 supplies uniqueness. resolvent_bound_of_bounded is the same statement with the compactness discharged
formalises

formalises clauses (i) and (ii) together, for the dual of H_0^1(Omega) on an arbitrary Omega: every continuous linear functional f is represented by a tuple (f_0, f_1, …, f_n) of L^2(Omega) functions, and the tuple norm of the Riesz representative equals ‖f‖_{H^{-1}} and is least among all representing tuples. Evans states the norm in (ii) as an infimum without asserting attainment, though his proof produces the attaining tuple; the declaration states the attainment. The sign convention differs: the representation reads int_Omega f_0 v - sum_i int_Omega f_i D_i v, where Evans carries a plus in every term
formalises

formalises the theorem for a compact operator K on an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space: 0 lies in the real spectrum, the nonzero spectrum coincides with the nonzero eigenvalues, the nonzero spectrum is countable, and for each delta > 0 only finitely many spectral points have modulus at least delta. Evans states the last of these as the disjunction that the nonzero spectrum is finite or a sequence tending to zero, which the countability and the finiteness above every delta carry between them. The manuscript cites Brezis §6.3 for this theorem; that text is not transcribed, and Evans' Appendix D Theorem 6 states it

formalises clause (iii) for an abstract bounded bilinear form B on H_0^1(Omega) that is symmetric and coercive, with the compactness of the embedding into L^2(Omega) as a hypothesis: the eigenspaces of the solution operator G span L^2(Omega), their orthogonal complement being trivial. Evans fixes the divergence-form operator with C^infty coefficients on a connected U and produces the orthonormal basis; clauses (i) and (ii), reality of the eigenvalues and their divergence to infinity, sit outside the declaration. symmetric_fullElliptic_spectral is the divergence-form instance
formalises
formalises

formalises clause (iii) for the divergence-form operator Lu = -D_j(a^{ij} D_i u) + c u with a^{ij} symmetric almost everywhere, b = 0 and c >= 0, over solutions in H_0^1(Omega): the eigenspaces of the solution operator span L^2(Omega). Evans takes a^{ij} in C^infty of the closure of U with U connected, where the declaration takes bounded measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients and asks neither connectedness nor smoothness, and admits the zeroth-order term c that Evans' (2) omits. The Poincare bound and the compactness of the embedding are hypotheses. As with solOp_spectral, clauses (i) and (ii) sit outside the declaration
formalises

formalises the admissibility step of the induction, for a weak solution quantified over H_0^1(Omega) rather than H^1(U): the cutoff xi times a first derivative of the solution is again in H_0^1(Omega), carrying its weak gradient
formalises
formalises
formalises the concatenation of the two embeddings at d = 2, where the Sobolev conjugate of 2 degenerates: the step is taken at p = 4/3, whose conjugate is 4, and Morrey then applies at 4 > 2

formalises the inequality in general dimension d and at a general exponent pair with 1/p' = 1/p - 1/d, transported from Evans' smooth compactly supported setting to a weak gradient on a ball by a cutoff and a mollification, so the bound carries the ball data ‖v‖ + sum of ‖g k‖ rather than the gradient alone
formalises the same inequality fed by data at an exponent q above p, the ball's finite measure supplying the factor |B|^(1/p - 1/q) that the constant absorbs
formalises
formalises the inequality at d = 2 and p = 4/3, whose Sobolev conjugate is 4, applied to L² data on a ball

formalises clause (i) iterated, on a family closed under weak differentiation in place of a single W^{k,p} function: L^2 data whose weak gradients are again members lies in L^{2d} on any smaller concentric ball. Evans reads the exponent off 1/q = 1/p - k/n in one step, under k < n/p; the ladder here takes d - 1 rungs of 1/(2d) each, which holds every intermediate reciprocal strictly positive and lands past d in every dimension. Membership alone is stated, the constant of each rung being absorbed

formalises clause (ii) at every order at once, on a family closed under weak differentiation in place of a single W^{k,p} function: on a smaller concentric ball every member has a representative in C^infty. Evans asks k > n/p and returns C^{k - [n/p] - 1, gamma} of the closure; with derivatives of every order available the Holder exponent plays no part, and the conclusion is smoothness on the open ball. The representatives are produced together, one per member, since the derivative of the representative of a member has to be the representative of that member's derivative

formalises the admissibility of Evans' test element on a literal half-ball, for a weak solution quantified over H_0^1(halfBall d r) rather than H^1(U): the cutoff zeta times a tangential difference quotient of the solution is again in H_0^1. Evans frames tangentiality as a constraint on the step h; the formalisation shows it is unconditional in h, and that tangentiality enters through the support inclusion tsupport (D_k^h phi) subset {x | 0 < x 0} The step is proof steps 1 to 3 of that theorem.

formalises the division by a^{nn} that recovers the normal second derivative. Evans performs it as pointwise algebra on functions already known to be twice differentiable; on L^2 weak derivatives the division needs the weight to be C^1 with bounded derivative, which a bounded-below bounded measurable weight does not supply The step is proof step 5 of that theorem, equation (55).

formalises the L^2 form of Evans' estimate (55) at the diagonal coefficient, with the lower bound a^{nn} >= theta of (54) discharged from ellipticity at xi = e_n and the derivative bound discharged from IsC1Coeff The step is proof step 5 of that theorem, equations (54) and (55).

formalises the theorem for a weak solution quantified over H_0^1(Omega) rather than Evans' H^1(U), and for coefficients in W^{k,infty} at every order rather than C^infty: the solution has a representative smooth on the interior of each compact V inside Omega. Evans states u in C^infty(U) for smooth coefficients and datum, which is an instance through IsCkCoeff.toIsWkInftyCoeff and IsWkInfty.ofContDiff. The conclusion names a representative, an L^2 class having no pointwise values, and it is smooth on the interior of V rather than on V, since smoothness is a statement about an open set

formalises the uniqueness of the L^2 weak derivative on R^d, the identification that lets a second derivative obtained as a weak limit of difference quotients be equated with the one obtained from the Leibniz rule. Evans states no such lemma and performs the identification silently. The development quantifies its weak solutions over H_0^1(Omega) rather than Evans' H^1(U); this lemma is independent of that choice, holding for any L^2 class on the whole space. The step is proof step 3 of that theorem, the passage from (34) to the reading of D^alpha u in (35).

formalises the replacement of the test function v-tilde by chi times v-tilde inside an integral whose weight vanishes almost everywhere off the set where the cutoff chi is identically 1, so that a localised integration by parts stated for test functions supported in the localisation region applies to a test function that is not itself supported there. Evans keeps v-tilde in C_c^infty(W) and never performs the replacement; it is forced by the cutoff that the H_0^1(Omega) solution space of this development, in place of Evans' H^1(U), puts into every term. The step is proof step 3 of that theorem, the integrations by parts that produce (34).

formalises the choice of the intermediate region W with V compactly inside W compactly inside U, as a second cutoff tower based at the topological support of the first tower's middle cutoff, together with the interior second weak derivatives of the solution on that region, as whole-space L^2 classes bounded by the data with one constant covering every direction pair. Evans fixes W and reads (31) and (32) off the induction hypothesis at m; here they come from interior_H2_estimate, for a weak solution quantified over H_0^1(Omega) rather than Evans' H^1(U). The step is proof step 2 of that theorem, the choice of W and the induction hypotheses (31) and (32).

formalises the passage from the identity B[u, v] = (f, v)_{L^2(U)}, which this development states through a bounded bilinear form on the trial space H_0^1(Omega) rather than over Evans' H^1(U), to the plain-integral form of the same identity on a measurable V inside Omega, against test functions supported in V, with each coordinate read as the V-restriction of its extension by zero. Evans moves between the two forms without comment. The step is proof step 3 of that theorem, the identity into which v := (-1)^{|alpha|} D^alpha v-tilde is inserted.

formalises equation (34) at |alpha| = 1 for a weak solution quantified over H_0^1(Omega) rather than Evans' H^1(U): on any compact V inside Omega the second weak derivatives exist with the interior H^2 bound, and the differentiated identity holds against every test function supported in V, with the datum delivered as the explicit lower-order sum of (36) rather than packaged as a single L^2 class. The weak l-derivative of f is carried as a hypothesis, since Evans (26) assumes f in H^m(U) and the datum (36) contains D^alpha f, which f in L^2 alone does not supply. The step is proof step 3 of that theorem, equations (34) to (36).

formalises the theorem for a weak solution quantified over H_0^1(Omega) rather than Evans' H^1(U), and for coefficients in W^{k,infty} rather than C^{k+1} of the closure: on every compact V inside Omega the solution carries weak derivatives to order k + 2, with one constant bounding all of them by the L^2 norms of the solution and of the datum's derivatives. Evans states the conclusion as u in H^{k+2}(V) with the estimate; the family indexed by lists of directions carries the same data, named so that the induction can hand a derivative on. The datum's derivatives are a hypothesis with a bound, where Evans takes f in H^k(U)

formalises Hölder's inequality at p = q = 2 on an interval, squared and stated for the signed integral: (int_a^b f g)^2 <= (int_a^b f^2)(int_a^b g^2) for f and g continuous on [a, b]. Evans states int_U |u v| <= ‖u‖_{L^p(U)} ‖v‖_{L^q(U)} for u in L^p(U) and v in L^q(U); continuity on a compact interval supplies both memberships, and |int f g| <= int |f g| supplies the signed form. The route differs, being the discriminant of the nonnegative quadratic lambda |-> int_a^b (f - lambda g)^2 in place of Evans' passage through Young's inequality

formalises the p = q = 2 case on a coordinate box Q = prod_i (a_i, b_i), over the solution space H_0^1(Q) that Evans also takes, with an admissible constant exhibited: ‖u‖^2_{L^2(Q)} <= L^2/(2n) · sum_i ‖D_i u‖^2_{L^2(Q)} for L the maximal side, that is C_P = L/sqrt(2n). Evans asserts a constant depending on p, q, n and U without exhibiting one, and restricts to 1 <= p < n, which at p = 2 excludes dimensions one and two; the route here is the one-dimensional inequality and Fubini, which asks nothing of the dimension

formalises the p = q = 2 case on an arbitrary bounded Omega, over the solution space H_0^1(Omega) that Evans also takes: some C >= 0 bounds the function part by the gradient part throughout H_0^1(Omega). Evans takes U bounded and open and restricts to 1 <= p < n, so p = 2 carries the hypothesis n > 2; the declaration holds in every dimension and asks boundedness alone of Omega, the constant being transported from an enclosing box rather than derived from the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality, at the cost of L/sqrt(2n) in place of the sharp constant

formalises clause (i) iterated at the full step and to a bounded depth, on a family closed under weak differentiation in place of a single W^{k,p} function: after s rungs with 2 s <= d, a member sitting s orders below the top of the supply lies in L^q on a smaller concentric ball, for every q >= 2 with 1/q >= 1/2 - s/d. Evans reads the exponent off 1/q = 1/p - k/n in one step under k < n/p, at p = 2 and k = s; the rung condition 2 s <= d is that hypothesis in the non-strict form the last rung needs, since at s = d/2 in even dimensions the reciprocal is zero and every finite exponent is reached. Membership alone is stated, the constant of each rung being absorbed

formalises clause (i) run to L^{2d}, which passes d in every dimension and is the exponent Morrey then consumes. The rung count is floor(d/2), against the d - 1 a half-step ladder needs for the same conclusion, and it is the count Evans' exponent relation gives: 1/2 - floor(d/2)/d is zero for d even and 1/(2d) for d odd, both at most 1/(2d)

formalises clause (ii) at finite order, on a family closed under weak differentiation to bounded depth in place of a single W^{k,p} function: on a smaller concentric ball a member sitting n + 1 + floor(d/2) orders below the top of the supply has a representative of class C^n, and one sitting 1 + floor(d/2) below has a Holder-1/2 representative. At p = 2 that order is Evans' k - [n/p] - 1 exactly. The Holder exponent is his gamma = [n/p] + 1 - n/p when d is odd, and one admissible choice from the interval (0, 1) his statement leaves open when d is even. The conclusion is stated on the open ball rather than on a closure, and it names representatives, an L^2 class having no pointwise values; the last component identifies the family's entries as the classical partial derivatives of one another, which is what makes C^{n, 1/2} read as the multi-index statement Evans writes

formalises clause (ii) at p = 2 against the supply of weak derivatives interior regularity produces: an L^2 class with weak derivatives to order m on V, and k + 1 + floor(d/2) <= m, has on a ball inside V a family of representatives indexed by lists of directions, each of length at most k Holder-1/2 and of class C^{k - |alpha|}, and each the classical derivative of its parent. Evans takes u in W^{k,p}(U) on a bounded U with C^1 boundary and concludes on the closure of U; the statement here is local on a ball and asks nothing of the boundary. The order k = m - 1 - floor(d/2) is his, and the hypothesis m > n/p is this one at k = 0

formalises clause (ii) read at the root of that family: the class itself has a representative of class C^k on the ball, Holder-1/2 there, whenever its weak derivatives reach order k + 1 + floor(d/2). This is the statement Evans writes for u, the multi-index form above being the statement for every D^alpha u at once

formalises the estimate at the critical exponent alone, and on an arbitrary measurable Omega in place of a bounded open one. Evans states the range q in [1, p*] for a bounded U, and his proof reaches q = p* by approximating u in W_0^{1,p}(U) with C_c^infty(U) functions and applying Theorem 1 to the zero extension, using |U| < infinity only to drop from p* to a smaller q. At p = 2 that first half is what this states. The seminorm is the ENNReal-valued one and the gradient is read off the graph coordinates, so the right-hand side is the sum of the coordinate norms rather than ||Du||_{L^2}, and the constant is Mathlib's Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev constant, which depends on the dimension and the exponent alone where Evans lets C depend on U as well

formalises the theorem at p = 2 on a bounded measurable Omega: every exponent q with 1/q >= 1/2 - 1/d, the critical one included, is bounded by the gradient coordinates alone, and the dimension condition p < n reads 2 < d. Evans asks U bounded and open and writes the range as q in [1, p*]; the reciprocal form leaves q below 1 admissible, where he starts at 1, and on a domain of finite measure those exponents are weaker still. The constant is Mathlib's, which carries the measure of Omega through the factor |Omega|^(1/q - 1/p*) that Evans absorbs into C

formalises the interpolation inequality for L^p norms in the ENNReal-valued seminorm, at finite positive exponents and with a real parameter theta in (0,1), the reciprocal relation written 1/q = theta/r + (1-theta)/s. Evans states it for 1 <= s <= r <= t <= infinity and u in the intersection of the two end spaces; the seminorm form asks no membership, since an infinite right-hand side makes the bound vacuous, and the ordering of the three exponents follows from the relation rather than being assumed. The proof is his, Holder against the splitting of |u|^r into the two powers

formalises the theorem at p = 2 in the zero-boundary form: on a bounded measurable Omega, with no regularity of the boundary and no extension operator, the embedding of H_0^1(Omega) into L^q(Omega) is a compact operator for every q strictly between 2 and the Sobolev conjugate, that range being written as the reciprocal relation 1/q = theta/2 + (1-theta)/2* with theta in (0,1). Evans asks a C^1 boundary and writes the range as 1 <= q < p*. His q = p endpoint is embL2_isCompact here, proved from a translation modulus, and it supplies the net this argument refines; the exponents below 2 are not formalised. The interpolation step of his proof is eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_rpow, applied between L^2 and L^{2*} where he interpolates between L^1 and L^{p*}

formalises the same theorem at the exponents up to 2, where no interpolation is needed: the embedding factors through the L^2 one, the finite measure of a bounded domain supplying the inclusion of L^2 into L^q as a continuous linear map, so compactness is inherited from embL2_isCompact. With rellichEmbL_isCompact this covers Evans' range 1 <= q < p* at p = 2, in the zero-boundary form that asks no regularity of the boundary

formalises the theorem at p = 2 over its whole range, in the zero-boundary form: on a bounded measurable Omega the embedding of H_0^1(Omega) into L^q(Omega) is a compact operator for every q below the Sobolev conjugate, where Evans asks a bounded open U with C^1 boundary and writes the range as 1 <= q < p*. The lower bound q >= 1 is the Fact instance the target space needs. The interpolation parameter of the exponents above 2 is recovered from q < 2* here rather than assumed, and the two halves are rellichEmbL_isCompact_of_le and rellichEmbL_isCompact

formalises the interval clause (ii) leaves open. When n/p is an integer, which at p = 2 is an even dimension, Evans allows any positive gamma below 1; the ladder reaches every finite exponent after d/2 rungs, since the reciprocal it lands on is zero, so Morrey reads off 1 - d/P and P = d/(1 - gamma) realises each gamma. contDiffOn_holder_of_gradClosed fixes the single choice 1/2, which is the forced value in odd dimension and one admissible value here

formalises the estimate of clause (i) at p = 2, on a family closed under weak differentiation in place of a single W^{k,p} function: one constant, depending on the dimension, the rung count, the exponent and the two radii and quantified before the family, takes a uniform L^2 bound over the outer ball to the L^q bound on the inner one. Evans writes the norm on the right as ||u||_{W^{k,p}(U)} with C depending on k, p, n and U; the uniform bound over the members the rungs consume is that norm here, and the domain pair is two concentric balls in place of a bounded U with C^1 boundary. memLp_of_gradClosed_fullStep is this with the constant discarded

formalises the estimate of clause (ii) at p = 2, composing the ladder's constant with Morrey's: one constant, quantified before the family, bounding the Holder seminorm of a member by a uniform L^2 bound over the outer ball. Evans writes ||u||_{C^{k-[n/p]-1,gamma}} <= C||u||_{W^{k,p}(U)}; the seminorm alone is bounded here, the supremum norm of the member being no part of what HolderOnWith records, and the domain pair is two concentric balls

formalises weak compactness for a real Hilbert space, where Evans states it for a reflexive Banach space: a bounded sequence has a subsequence whose inner products against every vector converge to the inner products against one vector, which is his weak convergence read through Riesz representation. The proof is the sequential one his reflexive statement leaves to Banach-Alaoglu: a diagonal over the countable family of inner products against the sequence itself, extended to the closed span by the uniform bound and to the whole space by orthogonal decomposition, so no separability of the space is assumed

formalises the existence of a constrained minimiser, with three differences from the statement as written. The constraint is the unit sphere of L^q rather than the vanishing of an integral of a general G, which is that constraint at G(z) = |z|^q minus a constant; the functional minimised is the H_0^1 norm rather than the Dirichlet energy, and Poincare makes the two equivalent on a bounded domain; and the exponent is restricted to q below the Sobolev conjugate, which is where rellichEmbL_isCompact_of_lt takes the constraint to the weak limit and where Evans' growth condition on G is spent. The domain is the unit ball, where the constraint set is inhabited by a renormalised bump

formalises clauses (i) and (ii): the infimum of B[u, u] over the functions of unit L^2 norm is attained, and a minimiser solves the weak eigenvalue problem B[u, v] = lambda_1 (u, v) for every v. The definition of lambda_1 as that infimum is the identity Evans writes in (5); that this infimum is the first eigenvalue of the operator is principalEigenvalue_le_of_weak_eigen. Two parts of the theorem are absent: the minimiser is not shown positive within the domain, which needs the maximum principle, and clause (iii), the simplicity of lambda_1, is not stated. The form is a general symmetric coercive form on H_0^1 with the Rellich compact embedding taken as a hypothesis, where Evans fixes the divergence-form L with c >= 0 on a bounded open set and has the embedding from the smoothness of the boundary

formalises the reading of clause (i) as a minimum over the eigenvalues rather than over the constraint set: any nonzero weak solution of B[u, v] = lambda (u, v) has lambda >= lambda_1, so the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient is the smallest eigenvalue and the name principal eigenvalue is earned. Evans obtains this from the orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions of Theorem 1 and the ordering 0 < lambda_1 <= lambda_2 <= ... that precedes the definition; the proof here needs no basis, being the Rayleigh bound applied to the eigenfunction itself. Coercivity rules out a nonzero element with vanishing L^2 class, which is where the divergence-form hypotheses are spent

instantiates clauses (i) and (ii) at L = -Delta with Dirichlet data on a bounded measurable domain, where embL2_isCompact discharges the compact embedding and the test-function Poincare bound discharges coercivity. Evans states the theorem for the general symmetric divergence-form L, so this is that statement at one operator. The eigenvalue named is that of the graph inner product on H_0^1, which exceeds the eigenvalue of -Delta by one, the function coordinate being a summand of the graph norm
